newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index plummets 1.61 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index plummets 1.61 pct at close.

text.p: The Manila share index plunged by 42.52 points, or 1.61 percent, closing at 2,605.65 points on Friday on continued foreign selling sparked initially by PLDT's drop in New York, traders said.
"Blue chips are being sold by foreign fund managers who are not so hot about the Philipines and the region," said Monique Lecaros, trading supervisor at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
"It's more follow-through selling on blue chips due to bad news that's coming out of the Philippines," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.

Traders said doubts on the sustainability of the country's economic growth, concerns about the property and the banking sector, poor first quarter corporate results as well as a cautious stance toward the region have created this bear market.

"We are not out of the woods. This is a market for long-term investors and there is no opportunity for those looking to buy and sell," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president for institutional sales at Philippine Asia Equity Securities.
Turnover was modest at 2.2 billion pesos since investors saw the May 1 Labour Day holiday as opportunity to take the rest of the week off, traders added.
PLDT which dragged the index down early in the session, closed 20 pesos lower at 1,485 pesos.
